subject: Appeal: Multi-cloud listing early-launch credit for Nebula Health pilot
messages:
From: Matt Reynolds <matt.reynolds@nebulahealth.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: Sara Li <sara.li@nebulahealth.com>, procure@nebulahealth.com
Date: Sun, 8 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood listing + early-launch credit request
Attachments: nebula_health_sku_matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet), pilot_scope.pdf (application/pdf)

Hi Soojin,

We’re excited to move the Nebula Health pilot to production and list the SKU across AWS Marketplace and Azure Marketplace for the US region. Our internal procurement team has asked whether Redwood can provide an early-launch marketplace credit to help offset onboarding costs for the pilot (expected 6 months, small committed usage initially).

High level ask: 20% listing/transaction credit for the first 6 months, plus documented co-sell uplift (we expect Azure/MS partner motion on their side). Nebula is ready to publish the offer next week if terms are agreed. Attached is a SKU matrix and a short pilot scope.

Can we get a quick read on whether Redwood can make an exception or propose an alternative? We need something formal to present to procurement by Thursday.

Thanks,
Matt
Matt Reynolds
Head of Cloud Partnerships
Nebula Health

---
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Matt Reynolds <matt.reynolds@nebulahealth.com>, Sara Li <sara.li@nebulahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Redwood listing + early-launch credit request
Attachments: pricing_calc_v2.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Ben / Karthik — looping you in. Nebula (DL-8472) is asking for a 20% early-launch credit across AWS and Azure for a 6-month pilot; they want to publish the offers next week. Attach is my working pricing calc.

Ask: can finance or deal desk approve a marketplace listing credit exception, and what guardrails do we need (commitment minimums, duration, co-sell uplift measurement)? Karthik — can marketplace ops publish on both clouds under a private-offer/PO flow quickly if we greenlight a credit?

Timing is tight; procurement wants a formal number by Thursday. If we cannot do 20% I'll need a counter-offer to present.

Background: Nebula is strategic in healthtech and could lead to a larger dedicated commitment H2 if pilot metrics look good. I suggested a time-boxed credit to reduce our CAC for the pilot.

Thanks — Soojin
So0jin Lee
Senior Account Executive, Marketplaces
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415 555 0123

---
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, Matt Reynolds <matt.reynolds@nebulahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Redwood listing + early-launch credit request

Soojin — thanks for the context and the calc. A few points from finance/deal desk perspective:

- 20% across both clouds for 6 months is higher than our standard early-adopter playbook; it could be acceptable with stronger guardrails.
- Proposed alternative (provisional): 12% listing credit applied as a one-time credit at invoice close for the first two months, plus a 10% co-sell uplift share for any Azure-driven net-new business discovered via joint activities for 6 months. If the pilot converts to Dedicated within 9 months, we can offer a retrospective additional credit to reach 18% total (subject to approval).
- Require: minimum $25k billed usage in the 6-month pilot window to qualify; signed MPO/Private Offer (AWS) or publisher listing agreement (Azure) with explicit credit terms; finance needs a short SOW outlining pilot metrics (attached pilot_scope.pdf covers most of this).
- Legal will need to sign a short amendment for marketplace credits; Hannah, can marketplace ops confirm whether we can publish both AWS and Azure MPO simultaneously and whether there’s any delay gating that would break the launch timeline?

If Nebula can accept the provisional structure, I’ll route to finance for a quick sign-off and generate a MPO template for AWS. Soojin, please confirm whether this is acceptable to the customer by EOD Thursday.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Marketplace GTM
Redwood Inference

---
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Matt Reynolds <matt.reynolds@nebulahealth.com>, Sara Li <sara.li@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 14:27:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Fwd: Redwood listing + early-launch credit request
Attachments: pricing_calc_v2.xlsx

Matt / Sara — quick update after internal review: we can provisionally offer a 15% early-launch credit (applied as a one-time credit over the first two invoice cycles) plus a defined 10% co-sell uplift for Azure-driven net-new revenue for six months. If Nebula hits the $25k billed usage threshold within the 6-month pilot, and then converts to Dedicated within 9 months, we’ll consider a retrospective top-up credit to reach 18% (subject to final finance sign-off).

Next steps for a formal offer:
- Customer to confirm acceptance of provisional terms by replying to this thread.
- We'll issue MPO for AWS and a publisher listing addendum for Azure; legal will prepare a short amendment and a DocuSign for signatures (link below).
- Nebula to confirm pilot start date and estimated usage cadence so we can lock the MPO window.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/nebula/DsSignLinkExample
HubSpot Deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DL-8472

If you accept the provisional terms, we’ll prioritize the listing and aim for a soft-publish next week. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
So0jin Lee
Senior Account Executive, Marketplaces
Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415 555 0123
